scope: GNOME/KDE Wayland portal backend implementation and protocol seam validation

commands.assertions: Portal Screenshot capture, RemoteDesktop session setup, key notification, stream-required pointer safety, and Wayland helper configuration pass protocol fakes.
Portal backend and helper configuration have no race detector findings.
Changed native, Wayland, helper, and host-desktop packages remain race-clean, including rejection when the bound D-Bus user session changes before observe, validate, or apply.
Changed native platform seams and existing X11/semantic/host-desktop behavior remain green.
Wayland backend compiles for the declared Linux architecture.
Lifecycle helper remains cross-platform buildable after adding Linux-only portal selection logic.
Lifecycle helper remains cross-platform buildable after adding Linux-only portal selection logic.

assertions: The helper accepts an explicitly named gnome or kde Wayland backend only when an active Wayland session is detected.
Wayland capture uses the XDG Screenshot portal and validates a file URI and complete bounded PNG before exposing pixels.
Input uses the XDG RemoteDesktop portal, with portal-granted keyboard/pointer devices and asynchronous request responses.
Absolute pointer actions fail closed when the portal does not return a stream identifier; relative motion is never substituted for requested coordinates.
Portal permission responses and malformed results are surfaced as unavailable or permission-denied outcomes.
X11 fallback remains refused for active Wayland sessions.
When an authenticated AT-SPI socket is provisioned, the helper composes it with the Wayland pixel backend for semantic observation without changing portal ownership.
Closing a portal-backed helper sends the generic org.freedesktop.portal.Session.Close operation before closing the session bus, preserving stop and input-release semantics.
Wheel actions first move the portal pointer to the validated observation coordinates through the granted stream, then emit bounded vertical/horizontal axis notifications.
The helper records the user-session D-Bus bus ID at startup and rechecks it on lifecycle probes, refusing a changed or disconnected bus.
Observe, Validate, and Apply recheck the bound user-session identity before using a portal grant, so a changed D-Bus session cannot reuse an old lease.
Named producer acceptance tests cover both NAT-06 (GNOME) and NAT-07 (KDE) portal capture and input flows using protocol fixtures.
The implementation uses the portal-defined a{sv} options arguments and device/type bitmasks for RemoteDesktop and ScreenCast methods.
RemoteDesktop and ScreenCast share one remote-desktop session handle when a cast stream is needed for absolute pointer coordinates.
The CreateSession response accepts the portal's documented string-encoded session_handle as well as a native object path.
Monitor sources are selected on the shared RemoteDesktop session before RemoteDesktop.Start, so returned streams are valid for absolute pointer notifications.
The implementation does not create a second ScreenCast session or call ScreenCast.Start independently; RemoteDesktop owns the combined session lifecycle.
Portal sessions carry unique path-safe session_handle_token values, preventing cross-helper session collisions.
Helper shutdown uses the generic org.freedesktop.portal.Session.Close operation required by the portal session contract.
limitations: No primary GNOME or KDE Wayland fixture with a completed user-session grant and control flow is available in this environment. A bounded nested GNOME compositor/AT-SPI/portal probe starts successfully but cannot complete PipeWire-backed capture, so NAT-06, NAT-07, and both live platform rows remain unverified.
Portal Screenshot is image-based; semantic observation requires a separately provisioned authenticated AT-SPI socket and has not received live GNOME/KDE evidence here.
